notes:
A holding page is no longer mistaken for a whole website.

Some sites answer a crawler with a short notice instead of their homepage — a
queue page, a "we are experiencing high demand" message — and do it with a normal
200 response and valid HTML. Because such a page links nowhere, Docket had
nothing left to crawl and concluded it had seen the entire site. It then reported,
with full confidence, that the site has no analytics anywhere, no prices anywhere,
and no About, Contact or Privacy page.

A page the site has itself withheld from search is not the site. Where every page
a crawl could read carries a noindex directive, Docket no longer draws conclusions
about what the rest of the site is missing, says the crawl was unreliable, and
stops claiming the report speaks for the site. Findings about the page it did read
are unaffected.

Internally, the rule for reading robots directives now lives in one place rather
than two.
